name: lldpd
why: A door into LLDP, the neighbour-discovery protocol your switches chatter over constantly, and almost nobody looks at it.

brief.what_it_is: lldpd is a Unix daemon and command-line tool that implements IEEE 802.1AB, the Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP). It sends LLDP frames out of each network interface and listens for frames from neighbouring devices, so a server or host can learn which switch port it is plugged into. The collected neighbour data is queried with the lldpcli command, as text or XML, or through SNMP. It runs on FreeBSD, GNU/Linux, macOS, NetBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris. It also partially supports LLDP-MED and some vendor protocols (CDP, FDP, SONMP, EDP).
brief.why_it_exists: LLDP is an industry-standard, inter-vendor mechanism for link-layer notifications, meant to replace proprietary protocols such as Cisco's CDP and Extreme's EDP. The homepage frames the goal as: "LLDP allows you to know exactly on which port is a server (and reciprocally)."
brief.how_it_works: The lldpd daemon uses privilege separation: a small root process handles the privileged work, and a second unprivileged process in a chroot does most of the work. The daemon both receives and transmits LLDP frames on each interface, and it can also answer with CDP, FDP, SONMP or EDP when it sees those frames. Linux kernel version affects which VLAN, bond and bridge information it can read through Netlink.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install: building from a Git checkout requires autogen.sh, configure, make and make install. Privilege separation needs a system user and group both named _lldpd (configurable at configure time) and an empty root-owned directory /usr/local/var/run/lldpd. lldpcli can run unprivileged if installed setuid or setgid _lldpd. The macOS route can also build an installer package with make -C osx pkg. Android requires the NDK version 22 or later, a hand-written compile.sh, and manual copying of files to /system, so it is a substantial job. Docker needs --net=host, --uts=host, NET_RAW and NET_ADMIN capabilities. The official website has the full installation guide, which the README recommends over its own text.
brief.standout: It is a small, widely deployed, open-source daemon for a protocol most people never see, and it includes an LLDP sender and receiver that also speak vendor protocols. The README's troubleshooting section is unusually candid about kernel patches, VLAN-tagged LLDP frames, and Intel X710 and ice cards that swallow LLDP in firmware, with the exact sysctl and debugfs commands for each.
brief.status: Appears active, but I could not confirm dates. The homepage lists version 1.0.21 and the GitHub README has a CI build badge. I saw no release date or last-commit date in the pages fetched.
brief.caveats: Windows is not supported; the README points to WinLLDPService, which is transmit-only. Kernels older than Linux 4.0 need the --enable-oldies configure flag for some functions. Bonding and VLAN behaviour depends on kernel versions, and some network cards need promiscuous mode or extra VLAN interfaces. Intel X710 and ice cards may need their firmware LLDP agent stopped. lldpcli links GNU Readline (GPL) when available, unless you configure --without-readline. Building for Android is involved. The core code is ISC-licensed.

The custom binary protocol between liblldpctl.so and lldpd is not stable. Therefore, the library should always be shipped with lldpd.
